text:
Anna P: Quick thought — we should add a Route Insight card that shows p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, error rate, and a token-waterfall split by kernel selection + KV cache hit/miss. Make regressions explainable at the route level.

Mike R: +1. How do we reliably attribute a p99 spike to kernel vs batching vs cache misses? Need a clear attribution method.

Sara L: We can emit token-level spans from the runtime. Each token span would carry labels: kernel_family, batch_size, kv_hit (true/false), cache_lookup_ms, compute_ms, total_token_ms. Aggregations roll up per-route.

Tony Q: That telemetry will increase cardinality and volume. We should sample deterministically: e.g., 0.1% of requests full token spans + always log full spans for traces that produced 5xx or latency > route SLO.

Joel M: We already have a token-latency waterfall in Grafana for some routes but it lacks kernel or kv fields. If we add kernel_name and kv_hit, we can do stacked waterfalls and attribution. Example prom-ish query for kv-hit waterfall:

```
sum(rate(token_latency_bucket{route="/chat", kernel_family=~".*", kv_hit="true"}[5m])) by (le, kernel_family)
```

Anna P: UI idea — waterfall stacked first by kv_hit (hit vs miss), then colored by kernel_family. Also a small "attribution" list: top-3 contributors to p99 with delta ms and link to sample trace.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: telemetry-agent v2.4 deployed to canary runtime nodes; it can emit token_spans with kernel_family + kv_hit tags. Enable via ENV REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=0.001 (opt-in).

Mike R: Kernel tag is risky for cardinality — we should normalize kernel names into a small set: {fast, compat, kv-optimized}. That keeps histogram labels low-cardinality.

Sara L: Agreed. Runtime will map kernel selection to kernel_family and bucketize cache latency into coarser buckets: <1ms, 1-5ms, 5-20ms, 20ms+.

Tony Q: Proposed action items:
1) eng-runtime: implement token_span schema + deterministic sampling + kernel_family mapping (owners: Anna, Sara)
2) eng-platform: define dashboard card API + attribution algorithm + backend queries (owners: Mike, Joel)
3) UX: mockups for stacked waterfall + contributor list (owner: Joel)
4) Rollout: canary + monitor telemetry volume + kill switch (owner: Tony)

Anna P: I'll prototype a minimal Grafana panel and a Console mock with the stacked waterfall and contributor list, then share queries in #eng-platform.

Joel M: Ping me when query PR is up. Also add trace link pattern in the card (e.g. /traces/<trace_id>) so customers can jump to full span.

Mike R: Draft attribution algorithm idea: attribute a slow token to the earliest component whose time exceeds a baseline threshold. Pseudocode: `if compute_ms > 0.7 * total_ms -> kernel; else if cache_lookup_ms > X -> kv; else -> batching/queue`. We should test on historical traces.

Sara L: I'll run a quick profiler sweep on canary to produce sample traces and attach a CSV with token-level fields. That will help validate attribution logic.

Tony Q: We need a cost estimate for storing token spans at 0.1% + error-captive full spans. Sara, can you calc expected increase in metrics cardinality and storage?

Sara L: Will report back by EOD tomorrow. For now, prototype agents will emit tags but default sampling = 1e-3.

Anna P: Thanks all — next step: I'll drop an initial mock and a minimal query set here in 24h.

Mike R: Nice. This should make p99 root-cause much less mysterious. :100:

Joel M: For visibility, moving this to a follow-up RFC if needed after prototype.

infra-bot: note: telemetry-agent v2.4 rollout scheduled to 10% canary at 2026-03-20T18:00Z.
